# Requirements Checklist: ART-008 slice 2 — Artifact Freshness

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing slice 1's standing
promises, the `Draft PR` row invariant, and the outcome-lines report are
complete, unambiguous, internally consistent, and consistent with the shipped
Phase 7 sweep contracts this slice inherits
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command. It
tests the *requirements*, not the implementation: every item asks whether
something is written down well, never whether code behaves.

**Filename**: `requirements-domain.md` rather than `requirements.md`. The
spec-template's own Specification Quality Checklist already owns
`requirements.md` in this directory and is a different artifact with a
different purpose. Appending domain items to it would mix a template gate with
a domain review; the two are kept apart.

## Scoping

The workflow prompt supplied the focus areas directly, so the three contextual
clarifying questions were resolved from it rather than asked:

- **Q1 Scope breadth** → The survival of slice 1's standing sentences across
  the slice boundary — the shipped promise passages, the recorded inheritance
  notes, and SC-008's guarantee — together with the `Draft PR` row invariant
  and the report coverage of the outcome lines on the stop and the proceed leg
  alike. Failure-report wording is out of scope (`error-handling.md` owns it);
  so is the join's ordering and idempotence (`state-management.md` owns it).
  Slice 1 sweep internals are out of scope (spec §Out of Scope).
- **Q2 Depth** → Standard, weighted to the three focus bullets, with the
  outcome-lines-on-both-paths bullet weighted highest per the prompt's
  "special attention".
- **Q3 Audience/timing** → Reviewer, at the pre-implementation gate.

Items already settled by `error-handling.md` and `state-management.md` are
cited to the closing requirement and not re-litigated. Four items the parent
recorded as settled — FR-027's removal of both promise passages, FR-021's
run-report sink at Phase 7, SC-008's file-level parity binding, and this
file's naming — are treated as decided and appear below only as citations.

## Requirement Consistency — The `Draft PR` Row Invariant

- [x] CHK022 - Is the sweep-never-writes-the-`Draft PR`-row invariant carried
  into this spec as a requirement rather than left in the shipped reference
  alone? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK023 - Does this spec state that the shipped sentence itself survives
  verbatim on both surfaces — that this slice neither rewrites nor deletes it?
  §FR-022 restates the rule but binds nothing about the shipped sentence, while
  §FR-027 removes two neighbouring passages and §FR-033b/§FR-015b/§FR-015d each
  mandate edits to shipped sentences. A reader has no statement telling them
  this one is left alone. [Gap, closed by FR-022 (revised)]
- [x] CHK024 - Is the sentence still **true** once this slice lands, and is the
  reasoning that makes it true written down? §FR-014's refresh causes the
  `Draft PR` row's cell to change during the sweep (§FR-039), so the plain
  reading of "The sweep never writes the `Draft PR` row on any path"
  (`phase-execution.md:1342`, `phase-execution-codex.md:1063`) is contradicted
  unless the reader supplies the writer-identity distinction §FR-022 draws.
  Nothing requires that distinction to be visible at the sentence.
  [Gap, closed by FR-022 (revised)]
- [x] CHK025 - Is the sentence's stated ground preserved by the reading this
  spec relies on? Its rationale is the corroboration gate's four stops — "a run
  that repaired the record it had just failed to corroborate would destroy the
  evidence of the discrepancy" — and the FR-014 refresh runs only after an
  entry-gate `match`, so no refresh ever repairs a row the run failed to
  corroborate. [Consistency, closed by FR-022 (revised); Spec §FR-016, §FR-034a]
- [x] CHK026 - Do the requirements agree on which commit carries the row write?
  §FR-022 states "this slice supplies only the commit that carries what the
  machinery wrote", while §FR-039 requires the write to ride the emission
  machinery's **own** record commit, "reused verbatim rather than a new commit
  shape this slice defines", and forbids folding it into §FR-018's commit. The
  two cannot both be right about ownership. [Conflict, closed by FR-022 (revised)]
- [x] CHK027 - Is the number of writers to the row fixed at one, with the
  identity of that writer named? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK028 - Is a second writer of the row excluded at the scope level as well
  as the requirement level, so the prohibition is not carried by one sentence
  alone? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK029 - Are the statuses that leave the row exactly as found enumerated,
  so "left as found" is a stated outcome rather than a default? [Coverage,
  Spec §FR-034, §FR-034a]

The sentence is falsified in the slice's own User Story 2 recovery case, and no requirement scopes, amends, or retires it. | **New FR-024a**: requires an added scoping sentence on both platform reference surfaces placing the one-line characterization on the per-comment dispositions the paragraph is about, and stating that the freshness evaluation contributes its own lines to the what-already-landed part on that leg. Shipped text is neither rewritten nor deleted, in the manner §FR-033b, §FR-015b, and §FR-015d already use. `plan.md` gains the matching surface-and-line row in a new "FR-024a's and FR-022's scoping edits" section. |
| CHK023, CHK024, CHK025, CHK026 | §FR-022 restated the invariant but bound nothing about the shipped sentence carrying it, left the writer-identity distinction that keeps the sentence true invisible at the sentence, and claimed a commit ownership §FR-039 assigns elsewhere. Three neighbouring requirements mandate edits to shipped sentences, so silence about this one reads as an oversight rather than a decision. | **§FR-022 (revised)**: states that the shipped sentence survives verbatim on both surfaces; names the writer-identity reading and the corroboration-gate ground that keep it true; requires the same added-scoping-sentence treatment so the reading is visible at the sentence; and replaces the false commit-ownership clause with the trigger-and-timing statement §Assumptions already uses, pointing at §FR-039 for the commit. `plan.md` carries the matching surface-and-line row beside FR-024a's. |
| CHK005, CHK006, CHK007, CHK008 | Slice 1's SC-008 constraint on slice 2 is a MUST NOT recorded only in slice 1's merged artifacts. This spec discharges it mechanically through §Out of Scope and §Assumptions but never records the inheritance, so a reviewer cannot confirm the guarantee still holds. The `SC-008` identifier means a different criterion in each slice, so the pointer slice 1 leaves resolves to the wrong requirement here. | **§Assumptions (new bullet)**: records the inherited constraint, names its source by slice rather than by bare identifier, states the inference it forbids, and confirms the fingerprint-protection premise the guarantee rests on is unchanged. No new FR: §Out of Scope already forbids changing the replies, so a requirement would restate an existing prohibition. No `plan.md` change: the constraint binds what this slice must not do, and the plan declares no work against the replies. |

## Notes

- **CHK019/CHK020 (FR-024a) go to consensus.** The requirement-level obligation
  is not in doubt — a shipped sentence this slice falsifies has to be dealt
  with, and this spec has already chosen scoping-over-rewriting three times.
  What is open is the *scope* the added sentence should state. Two readings of
  the shipped sentence are defensible: "one-line" describes the whole report,
  in which case slice 2 breaks a shipped guarantee and the operator-facing
  consequence needs stating; or it describes only the per-comment dispositions
  contribution, in which case the sentence was always narrower than its words
  and the added sentence merely says so. FR-024a takes the second reading,
  because the sentence sits inside the paragraph whose subject is the
  dispositions and because the alternative would put the shipped text in
  conflict with §FR-018a's restoration line as well. The choice changes what a
  reviewer is told on the recovery leg, so it is surfaced rather than settled
  here. Routed `[codebase, spec]` — the question is settled by how this
  repository's shipped reference prose scopes its own sentences and by the
  scoping precedents this spec has already set, not by any external standard.
- **CHK026's conflict is not routed.** §FR-039 is explicit and recent, states
  its commit shape twice, and forbids the two alternatives by name; §FR-022's
  clause is a summary sentence in a requirement whose subject is the row's
  writer, not its commit. Reading §FR-022 as authoritative would contradict
  §FR-039's "reused verbatim rather than a new commit shape this slice
  defines". Confidence is high and no second perspective would change it.
- **CHK023/CHK024/CHK025 are not routed either.** The invariant's survival is
  a statement this spec was missing, not a decision between options: §FR-022
  already commits to the writer-identity reading, and §FR-016 plus §FR-034a
  already establish that no refresh reaches a row the run failed to
  corroborate. The edit writes down reasoning the spec already relies on.
- **CHK005–CHK008 are not routed.** The constraint is inherited, not
  negotiated: slice 1 states it as a MUST NOT on slice 2, and this slice's
  §Out of Scope already complies. Recording it is bookkeeping.
- **Four items were settled before this run and are cited, not re-argued**:
  §FR-027's removal of both promise passages on both surfaces, §FR-021's
  run-report sink at the Phase 7 call site, §SC-008's file-level parity
  binding, and this file's name.
- All evidence is repo-local. Every line citation was read from
  `speckit-pro/skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution.md`,
  `speckit-pro/codex-skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution-codex.md`,
  and the slice-1 artifacts under `specs/art-008-feedback-sweep/` in this
  worktree rather than carried over from the plan's existing cites.
